# Agent Pi DSH compatibility adaptation

This directory retains the official AnySearch 0.1.8 package and its MIT license. The product adaptation is reproduced and verified by `scripts/patch-anysearch-alpha1.mjs`. The accompanying `AGENT-PI-ADAPTATION.json` records the reviewed source hashes (UTF-8 with LF-normalized line endings). [AnySearch upstream](https://github.com/anysearch-team/anysearch-dsh)

The product sets the DSH engine to 0.2.2-rc.1 and resolves the vendored plugin against the runtime's Cordis 4.1.0 and Schemastery 3.19.0. The adapter retains native search and fetch providers and advanced, batch and capability tools. A native search request capped above the provider's supported count is projected to ten results. Direct advanced requests outside 1–10 fail before making an HTTP request. Result content defaults to Markdown in the outer JSON envelope and also supports explicit JSON content.

The shared client resolves its configured credential reference for every request. The product settings use the existing DSH credential Remote to describe metadata and set/unset a value, without reading the key back. There is no claim that this existing local store is encrypted. A connection probe reuses the registered client and actual reference, including a customized reference. Saved credentials apply to the next request without restarting.

API key creation belongs to the service provider: https://anysearch.com/console/api-keys. The application does not create accounts or automatically accept credentials generated by anonymous quota errors. Upstream error text is discarded because HTTP 402 messages can contain usernames, passwords and API keys. Only safe HTTP status, authentication mode, a validated request UUID and recognized extraction error codes remain in diagnostics.

Official contracts reviewed:

- https://anysearch.com/docs/auth
- https://anysearch.com/docs/api-endpoints/v1-search
- https://anysearch.com/docs/api-endpoints/v1-extract

Search results require source review. Ranking alone does not establish authority, applicable jurisdiction or currency. The product research policy requests original-page inspection and material claim verification before professional conclusions.
